name: Bill Gates
role: Microsoft co-founder and CEO (1975–2000), philanthropist and chair of the Gates Foundation
summary: A technologist and philanthropist who does not identify with a party and seldom speaks on social or cultural issues. His public positions centre on innovation, global health and development, and clean energy (including nuclear power). He also argues for more progressive taxation of the rich, higher estate taxes and an active government role in research, aid and managing AI.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: In his 2019 year-end Gates Notes post he wrote that he favours a tax system in which people with more money pay a higher percentage and that the rich, including himself, should pay more than they do now. He proposed higher capital-gains and estate taxes and closing loopholes, while voicing reservations about the Warren and Sanders wealth-tax plans.

regulate-corporations.rationale: His views are mixed. As Microsoft CEO in 1998 he told the Senate the software industry did not need regulation. In his 2026 AI essay he rejected industry self-regulation of AI and proposed new public bodies to manage it. The rating reflects his more recent position and covers AI only.

cut-welfare.rationale: He has proposed taxing AI tokens and robots to fund retraining and the social safety net, which implies he wants to keep or expand welfare rather than cut it. He has not addressed welfare dependency directly.

state-harmful.rationale: He argues that government has a large role to play. He wrote that voluntary giving will never raise enough money for everything the government needs to do, and he says his foundation's goals depend on partnership with governments.

reduce-immigration.rationale: In 2008 testimony to Congress he called the H-1B cap arbitrary and asked for more skilled-worker visas, more green cards and no per-country limits. His public record concerns skilled immigration, not overall levels.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: In his 2026 AI essay he proposed an international organization to help manage the transition to AI, alongside new national bodies.

nation-first.rationale: His philanthropy rests on the principle that every life has equal value, and he has argued for foreign aid and against cuts to aid programmes. He has not framed this as a general position against national interest.

limit-growth.rationale: His 2025 climate memo argued that health and prosperity are the best defence against climate change and put human welfare ahead of temperature targets. He seeks clean-energy innovation rather than limits on growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He calls for large government investment in clean-energy R&D and called the Inflation Reduction Act possibly the most important US climate law. In 2025 he said climate change will not end civilization and that some money is better spent on health and poverty. This places him in favour of strong action but not of drastic measures.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Innovation is his main approach. He has said nuclear power done right will help meet climate goals and that AI will be fantastic for health and education. He has also warned that AI could become the worst source of injustice and that innovation matters only for the impact it makes possible, so he is not rated at the maximum.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He chairs TerraPower, which is building an advanced reactor in Wyoming, and has said nuclear energy, done right, will help meet climate goals with less waste and solved safety problems.

tax-inheritance.rationale: He has repeatedly called for raising the federal estate tax and closing the loopholes the wealthy use, and he says his own children will inherit under 1% of his fortune.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He has called for government funding of basic research and clean-energy research institutes modelled on the NIH, and supported the Inflation Reduction Act's clean-energy investments. In 2008 he asked for federal basic-research funding to rise 10% a year.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He treats economic development, energy access and technology as how humanity becomes healthier and less poor. His foundation's goals are about spreading those benefits, not rejecting industrial civilization.

accelerate-technology.rationale: He generally backs rapid innovation in energy, health and AI and has argued that pausing only the responsible AI developers would be counterproductive. He has also said he would support a credible global plan to slow AI, so he is not rated at the maximum.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He describes his philanthropy as aimed at the areas of greatest need and judged by the impact of innovations rather than the innovations themselves. His climate memo argued for prioritising by human welfare outcomes. The rating is inferred from this impact-focused approach rather than a statement about ideology.

notes: Gates Notes (gatesnotes.com) returned HTTP 403 to every fetch in this session, so his blog posts are cited through news coverage that quotes them (s2) and Wikipedia (s1). His views on regulation have changed: in 1998 he rejected software regulation, but in 2026 he rejected industry self-regulation of AI. His climate emphasis also shifted in 2025 toward health and prosperity over temperature targets. He has given little public evidence on social, religious or constitutional questions, so those are left null.
